results.note: The root command picked up Page's rustdoc as its about and long_about.

setup: The agent read the repository at commit 1013fe2 and built the README example and a clap-only equivalent in a scratch directory. The two structural cases came from a dependency map made after this run, and this run records them as not yet in place. The start and finish times are taken from the scratch files' timestamps. The first run's measurements did not reproduce exactly when the second run rebuilt the same commit, so compare the second run's paired figures.
summary: crumbkit's real value lies in failures whose recovery commands are checked against the live command tree, the output budget with batch cut-off, and the convention tests that run every suggested recovery. The rest is convenient but thin. A developer should build on clap directly unless the tool is agent-first with a resource/verb shape and can accept an unpublished dependency.
